papers_new.title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires continuous quantum error correction (QEC) to suppress physical noise. While Clifford-only workloads can defer corrections to software post-processing, universal computation breaks this paradigm: executing non-Clifford gates via magic-state gadgets introduces hard, real-time control-flow dependencies on error-corrected measurements. Consequently, the controller must extract syndromes, decode them, and update the Pauli frame in real time, closing the entire QEC loop within a strict $1\,μ\text{s}$ cycle. However, prior proposals on Pauli frame tracking remain largely theoretical, leaving the microarchitectural bottlenecks of tracking, resolving, and synchronizing frame updates across distributed control pipelines unaddressed. To this end, we present QuFrame, a control microarchitecture for real-time Pauli frame tracking that closes the QEC loop…

papers_new.title: General Noise Channels and Mid-Circuit Measurements for Pre-Trajectory Sampling with Batched Execution
papers_new.abstract: Many studies of quantum protocols require fast sampling of large amounts of measurement data from noisy quantum circuits, such as for training machine-learning decoders for quantum error correction. Exact simulation of realistic noise is expensive, while stabilizer-based simulators are fast but approximate, for example through Pauli twirling, which generally alters the output statistics. Pre-trajectory sampling with batched execution (PTSBE) accelerates exact trajectory simulation by sampling noise before state evolution. This method requires the outcome probability of every stochastic event to be independent of the state, which excludes mid-circuit measurements and general Kraus channels. We present a generalization of PTSBE to measurement and Kraus operators without approximation. Each event is partially pre-sampled, while deferred outcomes are drawn during grouped execution via…

papers_new.title: Fault-tolerant quantum processor with minimal external control
papers_new.abstract: Contemporary classical information processors integrate tens of billions of transistors printed on a chip, yet are fully controlled through comparatively few external wires. This is possible because data flows through hard-coded operations in step with a global clock and is steered by external instructions. Today's solid-state quantum processors are different -- every qubit receives instructions from outside the chip via its own dedicated control line, and error correction adds a further torrent of syndrome data that is transported off-chip. Here we show that the external control of a quantum chip can be greatly simplified. We propose a fault-tolerant architecture for universal quantum computation, inspired by modern classical processors, in which quantum information flows through a fixed, clocked device, propelled by local gates in a planar array. Our quantum processor receives an…

papers_new.title: Teleportation of Logical Qubits using Lattice Surgery with Superconducting Circuits
papers_new.abstract: Demonstrating a quantum advantage when solving large-scale computational problems on a quantum computer requires the correction of errors that occur due to limitations in control accuracy and coherence. Using the concept of quantum error correction, fault-tolerant logical qubits can be realized and manipulated with logical single- and two-qubit gates. In this paper, we experimentally analyze fault-tolerant lattice-surgery, which is a key primitive that enables operations between logical qubits realized in the surface-code. Using this primitive, we demonstrate the teleportation of logical states between two distance-three logical qubits realized in a superconducting circuit composed of 41 physical qubits. Throughout this process, we study the step-by-step transfer of logical information from a source to a target logical qubit by characterizing the time evolution of logical observables.…

papers_new.title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
papers_new.abstract: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains. Scaling from patch sizes of $3 \times 3$ to $7 \times 7$, we realize a timelike block suppression factor of $μ_T = 1.47 \pm 0.25$, demonstrating the ability to maintain temporal error suppression as the number of qubits increases. By extending the stability experiment for many cycles, we uncover a sum-of-exponentials behavior in error suppression caused by a temporally correlated error: data-qubit heating to the third excited state $|3\rangle$. We fully capture this effect with a parameter-free, device-level leakage model…

papers_new.title: Rate-1/2 Quantum LDPC Codes for Multi-tier Superconducting Hardware
papers_new.abstract: Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, while its resource overhead is governed in large part by the encoding rate, namely the number of logical qubits encoded per physical data qubit. Recent quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) constructions have entered the ultra-high-rate regime with encoding rates above 1/2, but their syndrome-extraction circuits generally rely on reconfigurable connectivity or long-range qubit transport, making them difficult to implement on fixed-connectivity superconducting hardware. Here we introduce Armillary codes, a family of ultra-high-rate qLDPC codes whose algebraic structure is generated by native iSWAP routing under hardware constraints. The construction jointly enforces stabilizer commutation and correct parallel syndrome extraction, while admitting radial and circumferential couplings in crossing-free routing layers.…
papers_new.excerpt: Quantum error correction is essential for scalable quantum computing, while its resource overhead is governed in large part by the encoding rate, namely the number of logical qubits encoded per physical data qubit.

papers_new.title: Proxima: Optimizing Syndrome Extraction Circuit Scheduling for Practical Quantum LDPC Codes
papers_new.abstract: The fault-tolerant performance of quantum error correction codes relies critically on the scheduling of parity checks in syndrome extraction circuits (SECs). For general CSS-type quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, the vast scheduling space and intricate error-propagation patterns make it computationally prohibitive to directly optimize the logical error rate (LER) or the exact circuit-level distance ($d_{\mathrm{circ}}$). To address this challenge, we introduce Proxima, a highly effective automated SEC scheduling framework guided by a distance-related metric termed proximity. Defined directly on the detector error model (DEM), proximity quantifies the minimum number of additional faults required to complete a seed fault to an undetectable logical failure, naturally capturing arbitrary circuit-level fault mechanisms and bounding $d_{\mathrm{circ}}$ from above. Proxima…

papers_new.title: Hierarchical Decoding for Quantum Error Correction
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system. Meeting these requirements at scale requires high throughput while controlling the end-to-end latency from readout to usable correction. In this paper, we organize decoding algorithms, execution strategies, and code constructions using common classifications and examine their performance and trade-offs under the reported evaluation conditions. We distinguish decoder-level hierarchy, where multiple decoding stages or resources cooperate to decode a single code, from code-level hierarchy, where the code construction itself introduces multiple decoding levels. We first review single-code hierarchical decoders and their cascaded predecoding and windowed, streaming, and distributed…

papers_new.title: An Architecture for Real-Time Quantum Error Correction with Neutral Atoms
papers_new.abstract: The latency of quantum measurement and classical decoding constrains the execution of adaptive fault-tolerant circuits. In neutral-atom processors, this requirement couples spatially resolved fluorescence detection to classical inference. Here we implement cascaded readout and decoding in a heterogeneous architecture that overlaps acquisition and processing at two spatial scales. Field-programmable gate arrays process camera rows as they arrive, while graphics processors decode an acquired logical block during acquisition of the next. This heterogeneous architecture offers flexibility in the choice of error-correcting codes and decoding algorithms. Direct communication preserves microsecond-scale transfer times for kilobyte payloads and supports interchangeable decoding algorithms. papers_new.title: Accelerating Quantum Error Correction Simulations under Coherent Noise with Compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product States
papers_new.abstract: Reliable assessment of quantum error correction requires understanding how coherent errors affect logical performance. Although tensor networks naturally capture coherent interference, entanglement growth and large qubit counts make repeated sampling costly. Here we develop a compiled Clifford-Augmented Matrix Product State (CAMPS) framework that reuses Clifford transformations across shots, recycles qubits released by measurements, evolves a compressed residual state, and accelerates sampling through rotation fusion and compilation tailored to the MPS layout. Surface-code benchmarks under fixed-sign coherent noise yield accurate logical error estimates at small bond dimensions, while random-sign simulations up to distance $d=9$ and on the $[[72,12,6]]$ bivariate bicycle code match the Pauli-twirling approximation results. Compared with uncompiled CAMPS, compiled CAMPS converges at…

papers_new.title: Topological Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers_new.abstract: Scaling universal quantum computation and implementing quantum machine learning with protected logical qubits remain challenging. To harness the computational potential of existing fault-tolerant quantum platforms, we introduce topological quantum reservoir computing, a novel approach using protected degrees of freedom for storage and the host system's intrinsic dynamics for information processing. Using a one-dimensional Kitaev chain, we show how long-lived Majorana edge modes and fast bulk responses support these complementary functions within the same many-body system. We identify the tradeoffs governing access to protected memory and show how matched interfaces enable programmable writing and interactions enable autonomous information consolidation from the bulk to the edge. These mechanisms improve performance on tasks requiring long-term retention of temporal information. Our…

papers_new.title: High-rate low-distance color codes
papers_new.abstract: Experimental implementations of two-dimensional color codes encoding a single logical qubit have surpassed the fidelity of physical qubits. A natural next step is to investigate higher-rate codes that encode multiple logical qubits. Here we propose small, high-rate 2D color codes for this purpose. We design distance-$3$ codes with encoding rates up to $1/3$ and distance-$4$ codes with encoding rates up to $1/4$. We prove that these rates are optimal for color codes with only color boundaries on surfaces with non-negative Euler characteristic. We benchmark the codes by simulating Steane-style error correction with real-time feedback and no post-selection in a linear trapped-ion chain model with all-to-all connectivity. The two best-performing codes have parameters $[[20,4,4]]$ and $[[16,4,4]]$ and achieve break-even at two-qubit gate infidelities of $0.22\%$ and $0.26\%$, respectively.…

papers_new.title: CHEQ: A Concurrent Hardware Evaluation Platform for QEC Decoders via Batch-Invariant Circuit-Level Noise Sampling
papers_new.abstract: Hardware quantum error correction (QEC) decoders require validation of logical error suppression and timing compliance before deployment. Rare logical failures and deadline violations demand extensive sampling, while algorithm-level software evaluation does not directly measure hardware response times. Circuit-level noise models contain many error mechanisms but few firings per shot at low physical error rates, making exhaustive per-shot scanning inefficient. We present CHEQ, an FPGA platform integrating on-chip sampling, concurrent decoder evaluation, scoring, and RISC-V control. Its Sampling Units use geometric skipping to sample firing locations from detector error models and amortize mechanism traversal across shots within each batch. Under independent random draws and exact geometric sampling, the shot distribution is invariant to batch size, enabling a memory-throughput tradeoff.…

papers_new.title: MASQ: Measurement-Adaptive Sampling for Near-Clifford Quantum Error Correction Circuits
papers_new.abstract: Classical sampling of quantum error correction (QEC) circuits supports fault-tolerant protocol evaluation, but estimating rare logical failures requires many independent shots. Frame-active-state simulators isolate non-stabilizer information in a dense active-state vector, yet dense-state processing remains exponential in the active width. This paper presents MASQ, an exact measurement-adaptive sampler for near-Clifford QEC circuits based on selective materialization of non-Clifford rotations. At each measurement boundary, MASQ materializes only rotations in a measurement-relevant closure capturing direct and indirect non-commuting dependencies, deferring the rest to limit active-state expansion. Stabilizer-assisted elimination further removes rotations certified to be invisible to all future measurements. A circuit-dependent schedule is computed once and shared across shots, while…

papers_new.title: Magic state cultivation with lattice-surgery escape on superconducting hardware
papers_new.abstract: Magic state cultivation (MSC) is a low-overhead protocol for fault-tolerantly preparing logical magic states. In this work, we implement two MSC variants to prepare a magic state in a distance-5 code on a publicly available IBM Nighthawk processor. The first is a lattice-surgery escape, recently proposed by Hirano et al. and experimentally studied here for the first time. The second is a grafting escape, previously demonstrated by Rosenfeld et al., and extended here by incorporating a switch into a matchable code. Both protocols begin with fault-tolerant cultivation of a T state on a color code, followed by an escape into a larger code. We decode the results using minimum-weight perfect matching or Tesseract on circuit-level error models calibrated to the hardware noise. papers_new.excerpt: Magic state cultivation (MSC) is a low-overhead protocol for fault-tolerantly preparing logical magic states.

papers_new.title: Probing the real-time decoding accuracy bounds in trapped ion architectures
papers_new.abstract: Fault tolerant quantum computers will rely on real-time decoders that process syndromes faster than the QEC cycle duration. The millisecond cycle times offered by trapped ion platforms relax low-latency decoding demands, but simulations and experiments have not yet exploited this time budget to reach maximum logical error suppression. We show how a hybrid sliding window decoding scheme composed of a lower-accuracy and a higher-accuracy decoder can yield substantially improved logical error rates, while preserving low latency. All windows are handled by the lower-accuracy decoder, with some windows being infrequently switched to the higher-accuracy decoder. We extract soft-output information from the lower-accuracy decoder efficiently for any QLDPC code, which allows us to identify decoding windows of low confidence. papers_new.title: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
papers_new.abstract: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry. We analyse three collection scenarios, reliable rounds, continuous broadcast and ordered capture, and test the Dirichlet energy $\mathcal E_G=\mathbf z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf L\mathbf z/N$ of the fused decision map $\mathbf z\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with late-graph Laplacian $\mathbf L$, against two thresholds. Hidden Matching uses $O(\log N)$ qubits on fused bits, but in reliable rounds and continuous broadcast, where nodes report $b$ sub-bits separately, a classical record buffer before it uses $O(N b)$ bits; classical methods need $Ω(\sqrt N)$ bits in the worst case. papers_new.title: TCBP-JOBS: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction Decoding and Noise Learning with Near-Optimal Accuracy
papers_new.abstract: Achieving near-optimal quantum error correction (QEC) decoding accuracy often requires computationally expensive searches that limit both large-scale simulation and real-time operation. We introduce trajectory-calibrated belief propagation (TCBP), which learns calibrated fault probabilities from BP trajectories, and jittered OSD beam search (JOBS), which uses these probabilities to guide parallel GPU searches. Across surface, color and bivariate-bicycle code memory and surgery circuits, TCBP-JOBS achieves logical error rates comparable to those of the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder at physical error rates of 0.1% to 0.4%, and up to 4.5$\times$ lower on the largest codes. papers_new.title: Closing the loop on memory: accurate, shallow and transferable decoding of quantum LDPC codes
papers_new.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes have attracted interest for fault-tolerant quantum computing because their high-rate constructions offer a route to reduced qubit overhead. Realizing this potential requires reliable decoding. Belief propagation (BP) forms the basis of many qLDPC decoders, but can fail to converge under circuit-level noise. Memory-based variants can improve convergence, yet selecting memory strengths that work reliably across different syndromes remains challenging. Here we introduce TEMPO-BP, which adapts each variable's memory strength to the evolving decoding state through local feedback. On the gross code at a physical error rate of 0.4%, single-run TEMPO-BP achieves a per-shot logical failure rate of 0.73%, compared with 2.51% for BP+OSD+CS-10. papers_new.title: Accurate qLDPC decoding under real-time constraints
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires reconciling the computational demands of accurate decoding with the stringent timing constraints of real-time error correction. We present Spatiotemporal Covariance-Optimized Parallel Ensemble (SCOPE), a physics-informed framework for real-time decoding of quantum low-density parity-check codes (qLDPC). By exploiting the spatial symmetries of bivariate-bicycle (BB) codes and the temporal regularity of repeated syndrome extraction, SCOPE uncovers a spatiotemporally covariant decoding structure and organizes the circuit-level problem into a layered decoding strategy. We further compress the high-dimensional evolution of belief propagation (BP) into a low-dimensional dynamical representation, revealing distinct signatures of successful and failed decoding and enabling early detection of unpromising trajectories. papers_new.title: Scaling Pêlagos: Multi-GPU Orchestration for Relay Belief-Propagation Decoding
papers_new.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires quantum error-correction (QEC) decoders that achieve low logical error rates under real-time operating constraints. These constraints motivate heuristic decoding algorithms whose error-correction performance must be evaluated through large-scale simulation. High-throughput decoding accelerates this evaluation and the exploration of decoder parameters. Using multiple graphics processing units (GPUs) is a natural way to scale these simulations, but naively distributing syndrome batches introduces host-side preprocessing and output-collection overheads that limit scaling. To address these limitations, we extend the Pêlagos relay belief-propagation (Relay-BP) decoder with process-isolated orchestration, parallel host preprocessing, and shared-memory output. We evaluate both one-gross ($[[144,12,12]]$) and two-gross ($[[288,12,18]]$) codes in a…

papers_new.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
papers_new.abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by…

papers_new.title: Quasi-Cyclic Qudit Lifted Product Codes with Almost Linear Minimum Distance
papers_new.abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes are a promising route to fault-tolerant quantum computation with low overhead, and qudits offer advantages over qubits including more efficient information representation, improved magic state distillation, and richer algebraic structure for code design. Asymptotically good QLDPC codes arise from the lifted product (LP) construction with non-abelian lifts, but cyclic lifts remain attractive in practice because the resulting quasi-cyclic codes have circulant structure that hardware decoders exploit, which matters especially for non-binary decoders with costly check node operations. We introduce a qudit generalization of the LP construction over cyclic group algebras, which extends hypergraph product and LP codes to arbitrary prime-power dimensions and yields quasi-cyclic qudit CSS codes for every stacking order. papers_new.title: Quantum-logic detection of rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecules
papers_new.abstract: Collisions between molecules govern chemical reactions and energy transfer across a range of different environments from interstellar space to the Earth's atmosphere. Despite their fundamental importance, molecular collisions have traditionally been studied through ensemble-averaged experiments which obscure the dynamics of individual scattering events on the quantum level. Probing single molecular collisions with quantum-state resolution has thus far remained a major experimental challenge. Here, we demonstrate a method for detecting individual rotationally inelastic collisions of single molecular ions with neutral atoms using quantum-logic techniques. We prepare individual trapped N$_2^+$ ions in their rotational ground state, subject them to a beam of helium atoms and detect isolated collision events through their effects on the motion of the trapped ions. papers_new.title: Quantum CSS codes: Decoder-aware multiobjective design and bound-certified selection
papers_new.abstract: Quantum error-correcting codes trade decoding reliability against the resources needed to measure their checks. We formulate Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code design at fixed encoding resources as a decoder-aware multiobjective problem. The objectives are failure probability under sector-wise degenerate maximum-likelihood decoding and check weight, the minimum total weight of an independent pure-type generator basis. For independent bit- and phase-flip noise with perfect syndrome extraction, deterministic truncation bounds support selection under a failure-rate constraint. At a per-sector error probability of 0.01, the bounds certify that a code encoding two logical qubits into 40 physical qubits meets a failure-rate target of 0.001 at check weight 139. papers_new.title: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation
papers_new.abstract: Quantum compilation on superconducting processors requires selecting a connected execution region whose topology and calibrated properties suit the input circuit. This choice constrains subsequent routing and influences the noise encountered during execution, yet aggregate hardware-quality metrics alone may not reliably predict the execution fidelity of a given circuit. Calibration updates can also change region suitability and trigger the rebuilding of calibration-dependent resource structures. We present CREST, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that evaluates circuit-region compatibility before routing. papers_new.title: Quantum Simulation of First-Quantised Chemistry with a Sum-of-Squares Representation
papers_new.abstract: Calculating molecular energies is expected to be an important application of quantum computers, but the most efficient algorithms to achieve this typically have significant space requirements. Scaling quantum processors to thousands of logical qubits is a daunting engineering challenge, so developing algorithms that run with reduced qubit requirements is of particular importance. Moreover, most algorithms are benchmarked on active spaces with about as many orbitals as electrons, missing dynamical correlation which is necessary to describe real chemistry. Capturing this correlation requires several times more orbitals than electrons, even in compact atomic-orbital basis sets. This low-filling regime favours first quantisation, where each electron is represented by a number of qubits that grows only logarithmically with the number of orbitals. papers_new.title: On Reaction Depth and Fast Fault-Tolerant Boolean Logic
papers_new.abstract: Reducing runtimes of quantum applications is critical for practical viability. On quantum computers, the runtime can depend both on the speed of quantum operations and on how often the program must wait for the classical coprocessor to determine adaptive operations. Some recent approaches to reducing this overhead have focused on minimizing the "reaction depth" of a computation, informally defined as the number of times the classical coprocessor must be consulted while running a quantum program. In this work, we formalize the notion of reaction depth. We find several subtleties in this theory. For example, we distinguish the reaction depth of a circuit from that of a circuit run, and show that the magic depth of a unitary can be higher than the reaction depth once compiled into Clifford computation and magic state injection. papers_new.title: Addressable transversal CCZ gates on almost good quantum LDPC codes and nearly optimal magic state protocols
papers_new.abstract: Assuming uniform subfield product expansion, we construct quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes with distances $Ω_ε(N/\log^2N)$ and at least $N^{1-ε}$ individually addressable logical CCZ gates on pairwise disjoint triples of logical qubits, for every fixed $0<ε<1$. With all logical qubits outside these triples initialized to $|0\rangle$, any subset of the corresponding logical CCZ gates can be implemented with a transversal physical CCZ circuit. As applications, we obtain two nearly optimal magic state protocols: CCZ distillation with arbitrarily small overhead exponent $γ\rightarrow 0$ and error suppression of nearly linear order, and a magic state fountain that directly prepares $N^{1-ε}$ encoded CCZ magic states with nearly linear distance $Ω_ε(N/\log^2N)$. papers_new.title: Parity Push Post-Selection with Soft Parity Constraints for Quantum LDPC Codes
papers_new.abstract: Post-selection lowers the logical error rate of a quantum error-correcting code by rejecting unreliable shots. For a code with $K$ logical observables, the logical gap, a standard post-selection criterion, involves $2^K$ logical classes, and existing approximations to it suffer from a non-convergence error floor or a shielding effect. We introduce a decoder-agnostic post-selection strategy for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, called parity push post-selection (PPPS), which re-decodes a shot once per logical observable with a push toward the opposite parity. Each push adds one check node and one variable node to the Tanner graph of the detector error model, and we accept a shot only when every re-decoding returns a solution in the original logical class. papers_new.title: Degree and normalization frontiers for bounded QSVT inversion
papers_new.abstract: Quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) implements matrix inversion using bounded polynomials. Increasing polynomial degree can improve normalization and reduce amplified query cost, with savings that depend on the error criterion. However, existing bounded methods either fix the normalization or work far below the condition numbers of fault-tolerant resource estimates. We therefore analyze this trade-off for absolute reciprocal error, which controls inverse-operator accuracy, and for residual error, which suffices for normalized linear solves. For absolute reciprocal error, we establish a scaling limit to a constrained least-norm problem for entire functions and characterize its high-accuracy frontier using elliptic integrals. papers_new.title: Collective Superconducting-Qubit Interfaces for Microwave-to-Optical Quantum Transduction
papers_new.abstract: Microwave-to-optical quantum transduction is essential for connecting superconducting quantum processors through optical networks. Mechanically mediated transducers, however, remain limited by weak electromechanical coupling, dissipation, and added noise. In this work, we study a transducer in which an ensemble of superconducting qubits couples collectively to a shared optomechanical resonator. For weak signals, we show that ensemble size and optical pump strength together set the conversion efficiency, added noise, and bandwidth, with pump heating limiting efficiency to a finite optimal pump strength. Near half excitation, the collective coupling grows nearly linearly with ensemble size, accelerating transfer of an excitation into the mechanics. papers_new.excerpt: Microwave-to-optical quantum transduction is essential for connecting superconducting quantum processors through optical networks.

papers_new.title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
papers_new.abstract: Ensemble prediction of nonlinear dynamics propagates a probability density whose linear transport equation retains the nonlinear drift, but grid-dependent circuit costs leave end-to-end feasibility in early fault-tolerant quantum computing unresolved. We couple polynomial reduced-order models fitted by sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to Walsh-synthesized Koopman-von Neumann (KvN) transport and surface-code resource estimation. At fixed model dimension and drift degree, per-step transport rotation counts scale polylogarithmically with cells per reduced coordinate. papers_new.title: Performance of Fusion-Based Quantum Computing with Imperfect Photon Indistinguishability
papers_new.abstract: Fusion-based quantum computation (FBQC) is a promising route to fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing, connecting small entangled resource states through linear-optical fusion measurements. While logical encoding can substantially improve resilience to photon loss, whether these benefits extend to other noise remain an open question. In this work, we show that this is not generally the case when accounting for partial photon distinguishability during resource state generation and fusion measurement. We develop hardware-motivated noise models to capture these effects and investigate their impact on fault tolerance in the 6-ring fusion network. We compare unencoded and Shor(2,2)-encoded resource states prepared using all-photonic and emitter-assisted repeat-until-success (RUS) schemes. papers_new.title: PRISM: A Logical-Physical Boundary Compiler for Dual-Rail Qubits
papers_new.abstract: Quantum computers can encode each logical qubit across multiple physical degrees of freedom so that errors on the physical qubits can be detected or corrected. A compiler must then translate each logical gate into native instructions, and one gate can have several equivalent realizations that interact through different wires. Routing moves those wires, so a realization chosen before routing can force SWAPs that another would avoid, making code expansion and physical routing a phase-ordering problem. PRISM therefore keeps each gate's realizations open across the logical--physical boundary and commits to one only when routing reaches a layout that can execute it. We formalize which physical circuits implement a gate, which respect the fault model, and which the compiler keeps, and define when a gate can execute under a layout. papers_new.title: Nonlinear function regression using quantum ensemble learning
papers_new.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence and quantum technologies have driven the emergence of quantum machine learning, yet imperfections in near-term quantum devices remain a major obstacle for achieving practical quantum advantage. In the absence of fault-tolerant machines, ensemble learning, which combines multiple imperfect quantum devices, may unlock new quantum computing applications. Here, we introduce two ensemble-learning algorithms, namely Bagging and AdaBoost, for enhancing the accuracy of nonlinear regression problems. While Bagging trains variational quantum regressors independently, AdaBoost employs a sequential training strategy and achieves significantly better prediction accuracy. By incorporating systematic feature selection into our ensemble learning algorithms, we enhance their predictive power for highly nonlinear functions. We further improve prediction accuracy…

papers_new.title: The speed limit of gravitational entanglement and the cost of noise
papers_new.abstract: Is gravity quantum? A proposed test lets two small masses, each in a superposition of two places, become entangled through their mutual gravity. Gravity is weak, so the masses must stay coherent for seconds while random forces disturb them. Here we ask how fast gravity can entangle two masses, and what noise costs. Without noise we find the maximum rate exactly: it falls as the inverse cube of the separation, and two positions per mass achieve it. Above a noise level set by the masses and their separation, gravity's leading pull can be imitated by classical signals, and every strategy is limited to a rate falling at least as the inverse fourth power. Exact, continuous error correction shields the masses from noise but hides them from each other: the best rate falls as the inverse seventh power, and six positions on a hexagon come within 10% of it at large separation.

papers_new.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
papers_new.abstract: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. papers_new.title: Specifying & Verifying Quantum Error-Correcting Codes
papers_new.abstract: Building quantum computers is challenging due to the noise that affects qubits. Quantum error correction tackles noise by encoding information in quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. These codes are often complex, increasingly found by computational search, presented in diverse formalisms with informal arguments, and hard to reason about algorithmically. Given that the rest of the quantum computing stack relies on a QEC code's properties for correct computation, we propose a formally verified foundation for QEC codes. We present QECLean, a Lean-based framework for formally specifying and verifying QEC codes. QECLean backs every claimed QEC-code property with a machine-checked proof, unifies the diverse presentations of codes in the literature through common abstractions, and makes new codes easy to specify. We present a new compositional technique, code combinators, for proving code…

papers_new.title: Metrological Channels Induced by Encrypted Quantum Cloning: Optimal-Probe Fisher-Information Broadcasting and Single-Use Operational Recovery
papers_new.abstract: Encrypted quantum cloning creates multiple individually inaccessible signal systems from which an unknown input state can be recovered by combining any selected signal with a shared quantum key. Here we study parameter estimation when a local sensing transformation is applied after encrypted cloning and before decryption. For the two-clone qubit protocol, a local Pauli rotation on one encrypted signal is shown to induce, after standard decryption, a parameter-dependent Pauli dephasing channel rather than a unitary rotation. We derive its Pauli-transfer representation and the corresponding quantum Fisher information (QFI) for arbitrary mixed qubit probes. We then distinguish raw QFI, which for an optimal decoded probe may remain simultaneously present in a decoded output and its complement, from decoder-accessible QFI, which is operationally single-use because a first decryption destroys…

papers_classic.title: Surface codes: Towards practical large-scale quantum computation
papers_classic.abstract: This article provides an introduction to surface code quantum computing. We first estimate the size and speed of a surface code quantum computer. We then introduce the concept of the stabilizer, using two qubits, and extend this concept to stabilizers acting on a two-dimensional array of physical qubits, on which we implement the surface code. We next describe how logical qubits are formed in the surface code array and give numerical estimates of their fault tolerance. We outline how logical qubits are physically moved on the array, how qubit braid transformations are constructed, and how a braid between two logical qubits is equivalent to a controlled-not. We then describe the single-qubit Hadamard, $\stackrel{\ifmmode \hat{}\else \^{}\fi{}}{S}$ and $\stackrel{\ifmmode \hat{}\else \^{}\fi{}}{T}$ operators, completing the set of required gates for a universal quantum computer. papers_classic.title: Superconducting quantum circuits at the surface code threshold for fault tolerance
Quantum error correction for quantum memories
papers_classic.abstract: It may seem inevitable that highly entangled quantum states are susceptible to disturbance through interaction with a decohering environment. However, certain multiqubit entangled states are well protected from common forms of decoherence as the quantum information is hidden in inherently nonlocal degrees of freedom. This review shows that this robustness is enabled by specific measurements on subsets of qubits, implementing a quantum version of an error correction process. Beginning with the basics, the latest understanding of the relation between this form of error correction and the concept of two-dimensional topological order in many-body physics is reviewed.

papers_classic.title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum error correction [1, 2, 3, 4] provides a path to reach practical quantum computing by combining multiple physical qubits into a logical qubit, where the logical error rate is suppressed exponentially as more qubits are added. However, this exponential suppression only occurs if the physical error rate is below a critical threshold. Here, we present two below-threshold surface code memories on our newest generation of superconducting processors, Willow: a distance-7 code, and a distance-5 code integrated with a real-time decoder. The logical error rate of our larger quantum memory is suppressed by a factor of $$\varLambda \mathrm{=2.14}\pm 0.02$$ when increasing the code distance by two, culminating in a 101-qubit distance-7 code with 0.143% ± 0.003% error per cycle of error correction. This logical memory is also beyond break-even, exceeding its best physical qubit’s lifetime by…

papers_classic.title: Suppressing quantum errors by scaling a surface code logical qubit
papers_classic.abstract: Abstract Practical quantum computing will require error rates well below those achievable with physical qubits. Quantum error correction 1,2 offers a path to algorithmically relevant error rates by encoding logical qubits within many physical qubits, for which increasing the number of physical qubits enhances protection against physical errors. However, introducing more qubits also increases the number of error sources, so the density of errors must be sufficiently low for logical performance to improve with increasing code size. Here we report the measurement of logical qubit performance scaling across several code sizes, and demonstrate that our system of superconducting qubits has sufficient performance to overcome the additional errors from increasing qubit number. papers_classic.title: Surface code quantum computing by lattice surgery
papers_classic.abstract: Abstract In recent years, surface codes have become a leading method for quantum error correction in theoretical large-scale computational and communications architecture designs. Their comparatively high fault-tolerant thresholds and their natural two-dimensional nearest-neighbour (2DNN) structure make them an obvious choice for large scale designs in experimentally realistic systems. While fundamentally based on the toric code of Kitaev, there are many variants, two of which are the planar- and defect-based codes. Planar codes require fewer qubits to implement (for the same strength of error correction), but are restricted to encoding a single qubit of information. Interactions between encoded qubits are achieved via transversal operations, thus destroying the inherent 2DNN nature of the code. papers_classic.title: Bulk locality and quantum error correction in AdS/CFT
papers_classic.abstract: We point out a connection between the emergence of bulk locality in AdS/CFT and the theory of quantum error correction. Bulk notions such as Bogoliubov transformations, location in the radial direction, and the holographic entropy bound all have natural CFT interpretations in the language of quantum error correction. We also show that the question of whether bulk operator reconstruction works only in the causal wedge or all the way to the extremal surface is related to the question of whether or not the quantum error correcting code realized by AdS/CFT is also a “quantum secret sharing scheme”, and suggest a tensor network calculation that may settle the issue. Interestingly, the version of quantum error correction which is best suited to our analysis is the somewhat nonstandard “operator algebra quantum error correction” of Beny, Kempf, and Kribs. papers_classic.title: Realizing repeated quantum error correction in a distance-three surface code
Quantum error correction for beginners
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) and fault-tolerant quantum computation represent one of the most vital theoretical aspects of quantum information processing. It was well known from the early developments of this exciting field that the fragility of coherent quantum systems would be a catastrophic obstacle to the development of large-scale quantum computers. The introduction of quantum error correction in 1995 showed that active techniques could be employed to mitigate this fatal problem. However, quantum error correction and fault-tolerant computation is now a much larger field and many new codes, techniques, and methodologies have been developed to implement error correction for large-scale quantum algorithms. In response, we have attempted to summarize the basic aspects of quantum error correction and fault-tolerance, not as a detailed guide, but rather as a basic introduction. The…

papers_classic.title: A Game of Surface Codes: Large-Scale Quantum Computing with Lattice Surgery
papers_classic.abstract: Given a quantum gate circuit, how does one execute it in a fault-tolerant architecture with as little overhead as possible? In this paper, we discuss strategies for surface-code quantum computing on small, intermediate and large scales. They are strategies for space-time trade-offs, going from slow computations using few qubits to fast computations using many qubits. Our schemes are based on surface-code patches, which not only feature a low space cost compared to other surface-code schemes, but are also conceptually simple~--~simple enough that they can be described as a tile-based game with a small set of rules. Therefore, no knowledge of quantum error correction is necessary to understand the schemes in this paper, but only the concepts of qubits and measurements.

papers_classic.abstract: Abstract High-fidelity control of quantum bits is paramount for the reliable execution of quantum algorithms and for achieving fault tolerance—the ability to correct errors faster than they occur 1 . The central requirement for fault tolerance is expressed in terms of an error threshold. Whereas the actual threshold depends on many details, a common target is the approximately 1% error threshold of the well-known surface code 2,3 . Reaching two-qubit gate fidelities above 99% has been a long-standing major goal for semiconductor spin qubits. These qubits are promising for scaling, as they can leverage advanced semiconductor technology 4 . Here we report a spin-based quantum processor in silicon with single-qubit and two-qubit gate fidelities, all of which are above 99.5%, extracted from gate-set tomography. Application of a Resource Theory for Magic States to Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
papers_classic.abstract: Motivated by their necessity for most fault-tolerant quantum computation schemes, we formulate a resource theory for magic states. First, we show that robustness of magic is a well-behaved magic monotone that operationally quantifies the classical simulation overhead for a Gottesman-Knill-type scheme using ancillary magic states. Our framework subsequently finds immediate application in the task of synthesizing non-Clifford gates using magic states. When magic states are interspersed with Clifford gates, Pauli measurements, and stabilizer ancillas-the most general synthesis scenario-then the class of synthesizable unitaries is hard to characterize. Our techniques can place nontrivial lower bounds on the number of magic states required for implementing a given target unitary. Guided by these results, we have found new and optimal examples of such synthesis.

papers_classic.title: Quantum error correction: an introductory guide
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum error correction protocols will play a central role in the realisation of quantum computing; the choice of error correction code will influence the full quantum computing stack, from the layout of qubits at the physical level to gate compilation strategies at the software level. As such, familiarity with quantum coding is an essential prerequisite for the understanding of current and future quantum computing architectures. In this review, we provide an introductory guide to the theory and implementation of quantum error correction codes. Where possible, fundamental concepts are described using the simplest examples of detection and correction codes, the working of which can be verified by hand. We outline the construction and operation of the surface code, the most widely pursued error correction protocol for experiment. Finally, we discuss issues that arise in the practical…

papers_classic.title: Quantum Error Correction in Scrambling Dynamics and Measurement-Induced Phase Transition
papers_classic.abstract: We analyze the dynamics of entanglement entropy in a generic quantum many-body open system from the perspective of quantum information and error corrections. We introduce a random unitary circuit model with intermittent projective measurements, in which the degree of information scrambling by the unitary and the rate of projective measurements are independently controlled. This model displays two stable phases, characterized by the volume-law and area-law scaling entanglement entropy in steady states. The transition between the two phases is understood from the point of view of quantum error correction: the chaotic unitary evolution protects quantum information from projective measurements that act as errors. A phase transition occurs when the rate of errors exceeds a threshold that depends on the degree of information scrambling. We confirm these results using numerical simulations and…

papers_classic.title: Realization of Real-Time Fault-Tolerant Quantum Error Correction
papers_classic.abstract: Correcting errors in real time is essential for reliable large-scale quantum computations. Realizing this high-level function requires a system capable of several low-level primitives, including single-qubit and two-qubit operations, mid-circuit measurements of subsets of qubits, real-time processing of measurement outcomes, and the ability to condition subsequent gate operations on those measurements. In this work, we use a ten qubit QCCD trapped-ion quantum computer to encode a single logical qubit using the $[[7,1,3]]$ color code, first proposed by Steane~\cite{steane1996error}. The logical qubit is initialized into the eigenstates of three mutually unbiased bases using an encoding circuit, and we measure an average logical SPAM error of $1.7(6) \times 10^{-3}$, compared to the average physical SPAM error $2.4(8) \times 10^{-3}$ of our qubits. Realization of an Error-Correcting Surface Code with Superconducting Qubits
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical technique for transitioning from noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices to fully fledged quantum computers. The surface code, which has a high threshold error rate, is the leading quantum error correction code for two-dimensional grid architecture. So far, the repeated error correction capability of the surface code has not been realized experimentally. Here, we experimentally implement an error-correcting surface code, the distance-three surface code which consists of 17 qubits, on the Zuchongzhi 2.1 superconducting quantum processor. By executing several consecutive error correction cycles, the logical error can be significantly reduced after applying corrections, achieving the repeated error correction of surface code for the first time. papers_classic.title: Fault-Tolerant Measurement-Based Quantum Computing with Continuous-Variable Cluster States
papers_classic.abstract: A long-standing open question about Gaussian continuous-variable cluster states is whether they enable fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation. The answer is yes. Initial squeezing in the cluster above a threshold value of 20.5 dB ensures that errors from finite squeezing acting on encoded qubits are below the fault-tolerance threshold of known qubit-based error-correcting codes. By concatenating with one of these codes and using ancilla-based error correction, fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation of theoretically indefinite length is possible with finitely squeezed cluster states.

papers_classic.title: The XZZX surface code
papers_classic.abstract: Performing large calculations with a quantum computer will likely require a fault-tolerant architecture based on quantum error-correcting codes. The challenge is to design practical quantum error-correcting codes that perform well against realistic noise using modest resources. Here we show that a variant of the surface code-the XZZX code-offers remarkable performance for fault-tolerant quantum computation. The error threshold of this code matches what can be achieved with random codes (hashing) for every single-qubit Pauli noise channel; it is the first explicit code shown to have this universal property. We present numerical evidence that the threshold even exceeds this hashing bound for an experimentally relevant range of noise parameters. Focusing on the common situation where qubit dephasing is the dominant noise, we show that this code has a practical, high-performance decoder and…

papers_classic.title: Achieving the Heisenberg limit in quantum metrology using quantum error correction
papers_classic.abstract: Quantum metrology has many important applications in science and technology, ranging from frequency spectroscopy to gravitational wave detection. Quantum mechanics imposes a fundamental limit on measurement precision, called the Heisenberg limit, which can be achieved for noiseless quantum systems, but is not achievable in general for systems subject to noise. Here we study how measurement precision can be enhanced through quantum error correction, a general method for protecting a quantum system from the damaging effects of noise. We find a necessary and sufficient condition for achieving the Heisenberg limit using quantum probes subject to Markovian noise, assuming that noiseless ancilla systems are available, and that fast, accurate quantum processing can be performed. Low-distance surface codes under realistic quantum noise
papers_classic.abstract: Experimental implementation of the surface code will be a significant milestone for quantum computing. We develop a circuit and a decoder targeted for near-term implementation of a distance-3 surface code. We simulate the code under amplitude and phase damping and compare the threshold to a Pauli-twirl approximation. We find that the approximation yields a pessimistic threshold estimate. From numerical Monte Carlo simulations, we identify the gate and measurement speeds required to achieve reliable error correction. For superconductor devices, a qubit encoded in a 17-qubit surface code demonstrates a lower error rate than an unencoded qubit assuming gate times of 5--40 ns and ${T}_{1}$ times of at least 1--2 $\ensuremath{\mu}\mathrm{s}$. Quantum Error Correction for Metrology
papers_classic.abstract: We propose and analyze a new approach based on quantum error correction (QEC) to improve quantum metrology in the presence of noise. We identify the conditions under which QEC allows one to improve the signal-to-noise ratio in quantum-limited measurements, and we demonstrate that it enables, in certain situations, Heisenberg-limited sensitivity. We discuss specific applications to nanoscale sensing using nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond in which QEC can significantly improve the measurement sensitivity and bandwidth under realistic experimental conditions.

papers_classic.title: Erasure conversion for fault-tolerant quantum computing in alkaline earth Rydberg atom arrays
papers_classic.abstract: Abstract Executing quantum algorithms on error-corrected logical qubits is a critical step for scalable quantum computing, but the requisite numbers of qubits and physical error rates are demanding for current experimental hardware. Recently, the development of error correcting codes tailored to particular physical noise models has helped relax these requirements. In this work, we propose a qubit encoding and gate protocol for 171 Yb neutral atom qubits that converts the dominant physical errors into erasures, that is, errors in known locations. The key idea is to encode qubits in a metastable electronic level, such that gate errors predominantly result in transitions to disjoint subspaces whose populations can be continuously monitored via fluorescence. We estimate that 98% of errors can be converted into erasures. We quantify the benefit of this approach via circuit-level simulations…

papers_classic.title: Improved Quantum Metrology Using Quantum Error Correction
papers_classic.abstract: We consider quantum metrology in noisy environments, where the effect of noise and decoherence limits the achievable gain in precision by quantum entanglement. We show that by using tools from quantum error correction this limitation can be overcome. This is demonstrated in two scenarios, including a many-body Hamiltonian with single-qubit dephasing or depolarizing noise and a single-body Hamiltonian with transversal noise. In both cases, we show that Heisenberg scaling, and hence a quadratic improvement over the classical case, can be retained. Moreover, for the case of frequency estimation we find that the inclusion of error correction allows, in certain instances, for a finite optimal interrogation time even in the asymptotic limit.
